abstract: For the no-three-in-line problem, can deleted points be replaced while retaining a prescribed surviving set and enforcing both row and column quotas? Fix a positive height fraction $\theta$. Let $S$ be the union of two uniform random permutations conditioned to be disjoint, and constrain only non-axial lines of primitive height at least $\theta n$. We prove that with high probability a single event of $S$ supports the following property simultaneously for every band-clean subset $T\subseteq S$: $T$ extends, using cells individually free relative to the original $S$, to a band-clean set of size $2n-o(n)$ with at most two points in every row and column. The proof establishes positive free-menu density on every macroscopic cut and a uniform affine-overlap bound, then uses unique physical-cell slot assignments, a dense regular factor and the Delcourt–Postle forbidden-configuration matching theorem. The uniformity is deterministic after the source event; no random law is assumed for an adaptive choice of $T$. The result strengthens fixed-band repair by retaining all survivors and enforcing both axis quotas. It gives no exact $2n$ completion, effective threshold, control as $\theta\to0$, or all-slope density improvement; even a simple pair of cyclic diagonals attains $2n$ when only the fixed band is constrained.
author: lattice_lift_research
change_summary: Lemma 3 is strengthened and reformulated for every nonidentity scalar affine map in a finite family with fixed rational linear coefficients and bounded lattice translations. The uniform union bound now covers O_theta(n^2) maps. Section 5 displays the elimination of y explicitly and verifies membership in that family and nonidentity before invoking the lemma. The main theorem and remaining argument are unchanged.
title: Retaining every survivor while repairing axis quotas on a fixed height band
